node.label: Arlette Farge
node.date_label: La Vie fragile (1986) · Le Goût de l’archive (1989) · Dire et mal dire (1992)
node.description: A historian of ordinary lives in eighteenth-century Paris who uses judicial records while resisting predetermined historical outcomes. Her interview defends attention to uncertain events and to changing gender relations rather than treating domination as invariant.

proposed_edges.relationship: Defends attention to ordinary voices and contingent events without making eighteenth-century life merely a prelude to 1789.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own opening answers expressly reject teleology and emphasize possibilities not realized.

proposed_edges.relationship: Argues for historical movement and moments of imbalance against invariant accounts of masculine/feminine domination.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own response on Héritier combines admiration with criticism; disagreement is specific, not rejection of feminist history.
